# slopvac

[![CI](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=push)](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Security](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/actions/workflows/security.yml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=schedule)](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/actions/workflows/security.yml) [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/slopvac)](https://pypi.org/project/slopvac/) --- [Quick start](#quick-start) · [CLI reference](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md) · [Rules](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/rules.md) · [Metrics](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/metrics.md) · [Triage](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/triage.md) · [Suppressions](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/suppressions.md) · [Configuration](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#configuration) · [Agent setup](#agent-setup) · [Writing guidance](#writing-guidance) · [Semantic review](#semantic-review) · [CI](#ci-integration) · [Roadmap](#roadmap) `slopvac` lints prose and source comments. Its rules cover AI writing patterns and general prose quality, including documentation discipline and technical-writing constraints. Use it on AI-generated documentation, PR descriptions, Markdown, and comments in supported source files such as TSX and JSX. Comment mode checks comments, not code or strings. Coding agents use the CLI to inspect findings and apply fixes. The same checks can run in pre-commit or CI for automated validation. ## Quick start Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and use Python 3.11 or later. **[Vale](https://vale.sh) 3.18 or later is required for a complete lint run.** Vale executes most deterministic rules and must be available on `PATH`. Slopvac checks the Vale version before compiling rules. Without Vale, lint exits 2 (incomplete) instead of 0 (pass). With Homebrew, install Vale and check the installed version: ```sh brew install vale vale --version ``` Other platforms can use the [Vale installation instructions](https://vale.sh). Contributors can run `mise install` to install the pinned Python, uv, and Vale tools from `mise.toml`. **End users do not need mise.** After installation, run `slopvac doctor` to check the Vale prerequisite. Install slopvac for persistent use with uv: ```sh uv tool install slopvac slopvac init slopvac README.md ``` Upgrade the installation with `uv tool upgrade slopvac`. To run slopvac without a persistent install, use `uvx slopvac README.md`. uvx reuses its cached environment. Use `uvx slopvac@latest README.md` to force the latest release. `init` creates `slopvac.toml` with the `normal` profile when absent and keeps an existing config unless you pass `--force`. Replace `README.md` with the file or directory to check. A passing run exits 0. Findings above a threshold exit 1. An incomplete check exits 2. ### Update notice If the cache contains a newer stable PyPI release, Slopvac prints an update notice after an eligible command. Slopvac refreshes that cache in the background. A newly discovered release can appear on a later run. Slopvac skips the check in these cases: - The command is `prime`. - The output format is non-text. - The report goes to a file or opens in a browser. - The environment contains `CI`. - Standard error is not a terminal. To disable the check, set one of these environment variables: - `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` - `SLOPVAC_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` - `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` ### Use the results ```sh slopvac --format json --out slopvac-report.json README.md slopvac --open README.md slopvac --fix README.md ``` `--fix` edits source files using deterministic replacements. Before keeping those edits, review the diff. The **[CLI reference](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md)** covers [linting and fixes](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#lint-documents), [profiles](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#profiles), and [scoring](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#scoring). ## What it checks The linter ships 168 checked rules across 26 categories. The catalog also carries 68 judgment rules that lint never reports. The [writing guidance](#writing-guidance) and [semantic review](#semantic-review) apply them. | Coverage | Examples | | --- | --- | | AI writing patterns | Repeated structures, inflated register, formatting tells, and generated residue | | General prose | Agency, word choice, scope, consistency, and promotional language | | Documentation discipline | Internal references, status language, and project history in user documentation | | Simplified Technical English | Sentence length, noun groups, procedural writing, and safety text | | Orwell-derived checks | Stale figures of speech, excess words, and unclear agency | The [rule reference](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/rules.md) lists individual rules and examples. Inspect them from the CLI: ```sh slopvac rules slopvac explain prose-craft.relative-date ``` ### Deterministic checks The native engine and Vale report findings with source locations. The report includes density per 100 words and a 0-100 score. Profiles and project settings control which findings fail a run. Missing or unsupported Vale, or `--no-vale`, leaves selected Vale-backed checks unchecked. Native findings remain available, but the run returns exit 2. ## Agent setup Slopvac installs small project-local files instead of harness marketplaces. The managed steering block tells the agent to run `slopvac prime`. Harnesses that load project skills also receive `slopvac-prose`. That skill directs agents to run `slopvac prime write` and `slopvac prime review` around prose work. Neither copies rule policy. The installed CLI prints it. Two commands write these files: - `slopvac init` creates `slopvac.toml` when absent and keeps an existing file unless you pass `--force`. Repeat `--harness ` to select multiple harnesses. Without `--harness`, it writes generic `AGENTS.md` steering. Naming a harness replaces that default, so add `--harness agents` to keep it. `--no-skills` writes steering without skills. `--skip-agents` writes only the config and rejects `--harness` and `--no-skills`. - `slopvac setup ` writes, checks, or removes one harness's steering and its skill when available. It writes only those files: it reads `[guidance]` from `slopvac.toml`, or uses the defaults when no config exists. Run it with or without `init`. `slopvac setup --list` prints each harness with its steering and skill paths. The [CLI reference](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#agent-steering) lists the per-harness paths, `setup --check` exit codes, and `--remove` behavior. ```sh slopvac init --harness claude --harness omp # config plus Claude Code and Oh My Pi slopvac setup codex # one harness; reads config, never writes it ``` Agents get detailed guidance on demand: ```sh slopvac prime ``` `prime` covers linting, exit-code semantics, Vale coverage, rule explanation, named exceptions, factual-claim verification, and writing, review, and reporting guidance. `slopvac prime report` prints an approval-gated issue workflow and posts nothing until the user approves the exact post. `slopvac onboard` prints a short setup handoff that points the agent to `prime`. ## Writing guidance `slopvac prime write` prints a writing guide for READMEs, docs, PR or MR descriptions, commit and release text, and specifications. The guide provides a genre table and a documentation contract. It also gives the `slopvac rules` command for the genre's judgment rules. `slopvac prime` tells the agent to run it before drafting or editing that prose. Disable it with `[guidance] write = "off"` in `slopvac.toml`. The [semantic guidance reference](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/semantic-guidance.md) lists every mode. ## Semantic review `slopvac prime review` prints a review workflow. The agent runs `slopvac lint` first, answers the judgment checklist for the document's genre, and checks factual claims against the code. The default reviewer pass uses one fresh-context subagent. The reviewer receives the text and the review output. For a revision, it also receives the original. It receives the source or brief when available. The reviewer runs lint and applies the checklist. It verifies factual claims against the source. Its report names each rule and quotes the affected text, with a proposed rewrite. It also identifies lost facts and claims stronger than the source. The author fixes or rebuts each finding. No loop follows unless requested. For a pass by the author, set `[guidance] review_depth = "self"`. For repeated reviewer rounds, set `review_depth = "adversary"`. Each round gets the findings the author rebutted earlier, and the loop stops when a round reports no finding the author accepts. If no subagent is available, the author runs the pass and records `self (no subagent available)`. `review = "ask"` asks before the review. `review = "off"` disables it. Slopvac only prints the workflow and the checklist. The agent's own model runs the review. ## CI integration ### pre-commit ```yaml repos: - repo: https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac rev: v2.18.1 # x-release-please-version hooks: - id: slopvac ``` The hook runs the `slopvac` binary on your `PATH`. Use `slopvac-strict` for the bundled `core:legacy-strict` style. The `--style` option is pending in the 3.0 CLI, so the hook command will change to the final option before release. Setup for prek, lefthook, and hk is in [docs/hooks.md](docs/hooks.md). ### GitHub Actions Add these steps to a workflow job: ```yaml - uses: actions/checkout@v7 - uses: srobroek/slopvac@v2.18.1 # x-release-please-version with: paths: README.md docs/ profile: normal ``` The action supports annotations and SARIF output, plus configuration and changed-file selection. See [action.yml](action.yml) for its inputs and outputs. ## Configure a project ```sh slopvac lint --explain-config README.md ``` The default profile is `normal`. Use `strict` for reference material or `relaxed` for informal text. Configure thresholds and rule severities in `slopvac.toml`, with `[[overrides]]` for path-specific settings. The [configuration reference](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#configuration) includes precedence and examples. See [suppressions and exclusions](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/suppressions.md) for a local exception or an excluded file, and [comment mode](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#comment-mode) for source files. ## Limits and evaluation A passing run means the selected checks stayed within configured thresholds. It does not establish factual correctness or make an overall judgment about writing quality beyond the configured rules. AI-signal labels describe rule evidence without changing the gate. Before merging a release PR, maintainers can run the report-only local [performance comparison](packages/slopvac-lint/docs/performance.md#pre-release-regression-comparison) on an idle host. It reports regressions and exits 0. Set `PERF_FAIL=1` to fail on them. ## Roadmap ## Agentic judgment Lint is deterministic, and the [semantic review](#semantic-review) is a checklist that an agent applies. A separate development track evaluates optional **typed judge models** for semantic decisions. Candidate backends include hosted [Jev](https://www.typesafeai.org/jev) and local/open models such as [Laya](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya), [Nimble](https://github.com/bespokelabsai/nimble), and [Kev](https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev), plus the [SemIf](https://github.com/theoleecj/semif) direct-logit scoring approach. The design appears in [issue #162](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/issues/162). The proposed layer would run **after** Slopvac parses the document and generates candidate spans. It has two uses: 1. **Semantic detection.** For AI/style defects that cannot be expressed reliably as syntax, structure, or fixed patterns, a typed judge evaluates bounded questions such as applicability, semantic fit, evidence sufficiency, and repair category. Slopvac code, not the model, derives the final confirm/reject/uncertain policy. 2. **Rule validation.** The provider receives a finding's rule id, exact source span, and local context. It assesses whether the trigger matches the intended defect. These assessments would measure false positives and validate rule changes against gold/control corpora. They would also identify deterministic triggers to improve. An optional local reranker may sit before the typed judge when candidate volume is high. The first candidate is [Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B). It can prioritize likely candidates to reduce judge cost, but the typed judge and deterministic host policy remain authoritative. The intended shape is: ```text source -> deterministic parsing and candidate generation -> optional recall-first local reranker -> typed decision provider -> deterministic host policy -> semantic detection / rule-validation report ``` Exact source locations remain host-authoritative. The semantic layer remains separate from the current linter CLI and its exit status. ## Contributing and security See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development and pull request guidance. Use [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report vulnerabilities in private. File bugs, rule findings, and proposals with an [issue form](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/issues/new/choose). Do not post security reports as issues. ## License Apache-2.0. Includes rules derived from [hardikpandya/stop-slop](https://github.com/hardikpandya/stop-slop) (MIT). See [sources](packages/slopvac-lint/README.md#sources) for rule provenance.

# Contributing

## Development setup

Install the pinned development tools and project dependencies from the repository root:

```sh
mise install
uv sync --extra dev
```

`mise.toml` pins Python, uv, Vale, and other development tools. The project supports Python 3.11 or later. Vale 3.18 or later enables complete linting. Run `mise install` to install pinned tools.

Run the test suite from the repository root:

```sh
mise exec -- uv run pytest
```

Run it through `mise exec --` so `vale` resolves to the version pinned in `mise.toml`. Tests marked `vale` run only when a `vale` is on `PATH`. If the `vale` on `PATH` is not the pin (for example a Homebrew install), the run stops with a usage error. CI installs the same pin.

The root `pyproject.toml` configures pytest to discover `packages/slopvac-lint/tests` and `tests`. CI runs the full suite with `python -m pytest` from the repository root. For documentation changes, CI runs the Slopvac prose gate and Markdown checks.

## Rust workspace

The 3.0 engine is a Cargo workspace under `crates/`. It sits beside the Python package, which stays the reference implementation. `rust-toolchain.toml` pins the toolchain, and `mise install` adds cargo-nextest. Run these from the repository root:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --no-tests=pass
```

A new crate needs a `Cargo.lock` entry in `extra-files` in `release-please-config.json`, or the release PR does not bump its version.

## Prose checks

Run Slopvac's repository prose gate on the files you changed:

```sh
uvx --from ./packages/slopvac-lint slopvac <files>
```

Exit 2 means the check is incomplete, not clean. If the command exits 2, install Vale 3.18 or later and rerun it. Fix findings before you open a pull request.

### Review comments on pull requests

CI also posts prose and shellcheck findings as review comments on added lines. The lint jobs in `lint.yml` run with read-only permissions and upload their findings as `reviewdog-*` artifacts. Then `reviewdog.yml` runs on `workflow_run` from the default branch, with `pull-requests: write`. It runs without any pull request code, so it works the same for pull requests from forks.

That workflow treats the artifacts as untrusted. It accepts a pull request number only when that PR is open and its head commit is the one the CI run tested. `workflow_run` workflows load from the default branch, so changes to `reviewdog.yml` take effect only after merge. The pass or fail result of the lint jobs does not depend on this path.

## Rules

Rule definitions live in [`packages/slopvac-lint/src/slopvac/rules/`](packages/slopvac-lint/src/slopvac/rules/). Each YAML file defines a category and its rules. Add examples of text the rule should flag and text it should leave alone.

Run the ruleset tests after changing examples:

```sh
mise exec -- uv run pytest packages/slopvac-lint/tests/test_ruleset.py
```

These tests check that each lexical rule's `bad` example matches its pattern. A `good` example must not match. The tests check that each lexical rule has an example. For substitutions, the tests check that each example resolves to a replacement.

## Stable releases and release candidates

Merge the release PR. Then run `just release X.Y.Z` to start publishing from
the matching `vX.Y.Z` tag. The workflow waits for approval in the `pypi`
environment before it publishes to PyPI.

Release candidates build from each update to the release PR branch. They also
wait for `pypi` approval. They get no tag or changelog entry.

Plain installs and `slopvac@latest` stay on the latest stable release. The package README lists how to opt in to a candidate.

## Commits and pull requests

Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). Release-please reads the commit message to prepare releases. Examples: `feat(rules): add a rule`, `fix: correct a rule`, and `docs: clarify setup`.

Open a pull request with a concise description and a list of checks you ran. CI must pass before merge. Maintainers squash-merge pull requests.

## Report a problem or propose a rule

Choose an issue form at [New issue](https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/issues/new/choose):

The forms cover these categories:

- **Bug:** Covers crashes, tracebacks, wrong exit codes, wrong or unstable output, or config, setup, init, Vale, cache, or prime defects.
- **False positive:** Covers text that a rule flags as slop incorrectly.
- **Missed slop:** Covers slop that no finding reports but an existing rule should catch. Use this form if unsure.
- **Mis-tagged:** Covers a finding on slop with the wrong rule, severity, or span/location.
- **Wrong fix:** Covers a correct match with a wrong message, replacement, or fix guidance. Use this form if `--fix` changes meaning or produces broken text.
- **New rule:** Covers a writing pattern that no existing rule detects.
- **Rule improvement:** Covers whole-rule changes to accuracy, examples, exceptions, judgment, tier, severity, genre advice, wording, or docs.

Before submitting an agent report, run `slopvac prime report`. Get the user's approval for the exact post.

Do not include paths, file names, or private data.
Do not include user names, host names, repository names, or organisation names.
Paste sample text into the report. A local file path is not enough.
Prefer a synthetic sample over text from private or proprietary sources.
Record the agent product name. Record the active model exactly as the harness reports it in its system prompt, context, or `/model` selection. Do not use model self-description or config defaults. Write N/A when the active model is unavailable.
Get the harness version from its version command. Write N/A when unavailable.
Do not infer these fields from environment variables.

# Slopvac 3.0 plan

Status: approved direction, 2026-11-14. Beads epic `slopvac-8l4`, labelled `slopvac-3.0`, tracks the work.
This document records the decisions, the evidence behind them, and the order of work.
slopvac 3.0 is a Rust rewrite with a public data and plugin API. It also absorbs the fixes that were meant for 2.x, because no further 2.x release ships.

## Inputs

- GitHub issues #252 to #257 from the Mecatl documentation trial, and the open dependency PRs.
- A Slack thread with the same reporter: trial results, model evaluations, and integration feedback.
- Experiments run on 2026-11-14. Their outputs stay out of the repository. The closed evidence beads in the table below record each method and result.

## Evidence summary

Labels in these experiments are single-annotator, and several samples are small. Treat the figures as estimates for these corpora.

| Experiment (bead) | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Stacklok page, before and after, default and trial config (`slopvac-8l4.2.13`) | Reproduces the reporter's scores. One false-positive error fails the gate: `negative-inventory-core` on the phrase `excluded from` in a constraint. | Fix the rule in the Python reference. Keep the page as an Apache-2.0 regression fixture. |
| Detector prototype, 92 public docs, 181k words (`slopvac-8l4.2.14`) | Correct findings: history-narration 5 of 175, negative-inventory 0 of 6, condition-after-command about 17%, title-case 225 of 280. Neither the `requirement` nor the sentence-level `enforced-invariant` detector removed an observed true positive. A lexical security tagger marked 40% of security-doc sentences. | Adopt `requirement`, `enforced-invariant`, and `change-note` contexts. Security context is declared, not inferred. |
| Rust regex spike, 143 compiled patterns, 8,496 texts (`slopvac-8l4.2.15`) | After two Unicode escapes were rewritten, PCRE2 with JIT matched Python on 142 patterns. One lookbehind failed to compile. PCRE2 ran about 4.5 times faster on one thread and about 40 times faster on 14 threads. Newline and case-folding edge cases are untested. | Use PCRE2. Bound the one variable-length lookbehind in `prose-craft.future-tense`. |
| Similarity A/B, lexical against model2vec, 40 docs, three rewrite replicates (`slopvac-8l4.2.16`) | Lexical matched or beat model2vec on alignment, dropped facts, and claim grouping. Dropped-fact F1 was 0.10 to 0.18 higher with lexical. A literal and negation diff found changed literals for review. | Lexical only. No embedding model in 3.0. |
| OCI spike: hand-rolled client on ureq, `oci-client`, smol (`slopvac-8l4.2.17`) | The ureq client pulls from GHCR in about 250 lines and adds 1.7 MB. `oci-client` adds 5.4 MB and needs tokio. smol shortened the subprocess prototype by about 20 lines but added 40 dependencies, and HTTP stayed blocking. GHCR has no referrers API. | Hand-rolled OCI client. No async runtime. Signatures ship as manifest layers. |
| rumdl and reviewdog evaluation (`slopvac-8l4.2.18`) | rumdl reports style, not slop: about 95% of 7,806 corpus findings are style or flavor noise. reviewdog parsed slopvac rdjsonl and SARIF locally. | Mention rumdl in docs only. Adopt reviewdog for PR reporting. |
| Rust crate research | Among the crates evaluated, none gave per-value provenance with line numbers, front matter with value spans, or install-method detection. | Write these. |
| Config spike: `schematic` against a layer stack of our own (`slopvac-8l4.4.1`) | Both resolve 10,000 files in under 9 µs each. `schematic` cannot show where each list element came from, gives no spans for YAML errors, and crashes on a cyclic `extends`. It adds 54 crates and 1.64 MB. | A layer stack of our own, which keeps file, line, and column for every contribution. |
| Diagram prototype: 37 human Mermaid blocks, 82 draw.io files, 61 LLM Mermaid diagrams (`slopvac-8l4.10.1`) | Default Sonnet output did not over-explain in this sample. 8 of 20 diagrams from a verbose prompt did. Maximum label length separated verbose diagrams from human ones (AUC 0.93). Token coverage flagged 14 of 14 redundant-prose cases, but only three human diagrams had prose to score. | Experimental lint rules for long labels, long notes, and prose that restates labels. Judgement rules for the rest. |

## Fixes rolled into 3.0

No 2.18.x or 2.19 release ships. The epic "Fixes rolled into 3.0" holds the fixes.

**Rule-data fixes in the Python reference.** These land on `main` without a release. The golden suite then records the fixed behavior, and the rule YAML carries into 3.0.

- #257 title case: count only words that start with one capital, then lower case. Skip acronyms, CamelCase, and project terms.
- #255: split "no longer" into its own rule that fires before change verbs only.
- #254: skip headings and table cells, and require an imperative opener.
- `negative-inventory-core`: fire on inventory forms only, and add the `requirement` exception.
- #256: accept the `versioned-change-note` exception.
- Bound the `future-tense` lookbehind. Hoist shared boundaries in the substitution and token pattern builders.

**Fixes the Rust beads own.** The 2.x beads for these are superseded by 3.0 beads that carry each requirement:

- #253 symlinks outside lint targets.
- #252: the `judgement` checklist honors config, error text keeps every interpolated value, and `prime write` reflects config.
- Update notices reach agents.
- `--format rdjsonl`.
- A warning for `[[overrides]]` globs that match nothing.
- STE stays out of the default behavior.
- release-please covers the Cargo workspace.

**Repository hygiene, to do now.**

- Dependabot only: remove `renovate.json`. Auto-merge patch updates and security updates with `dependabot/fetch-metadata` and the release app token. A weekly workflow checks the mise and Vale pins.
- Triage the open PRs. Close #245, #246, and #191 without merging: 3.0 removes Vale and ships a Rust binary.
- Adopt reviewdog in this repository, with a read-only lint job and a separate reporting job. Until 3.0 adds rdjsonl, reviewdog reads the 2.x SARIF output.

Python-only work is closed as not needed. That covers the standard-library swaps, Vale 3.27 support, and Python 3.15 classifiers.
When 3.0 ships, a bead tracks the replies on #252 to #257 and the Slack thread.

## 3.0 architecture

### Language and runtime

- **Language:** Rust, in a Cargo workspace. The Python 2.x code is the reference implementation until the golden suite passes.
- **Concurrency:** no async runtime. rayon handles CPU work. Dedicated threads handle waiting work. crossbeam-channel connects them, and `select!` with deadlines handles timeouts. ureq handles HTTP.
- **Engine:** slopvac matches every rule itself, and Vale is removed entirely. The README keeps an "Inspired by Vale" section that thanks the project.

| Concern | Choice |
|---|---|
| Regex | `pcre2` (JIT, match limits). The `regex` crate is optional for patterns without lookaround. |
| Word lists | `aho-corasick` |
| Markdown | `pulldown-cmark`. `markdown-rs` for MDX. A pre-pass masks `:::` and `!!!` containers. |
| Front matter | A new generic crate, `frontmatter-spans`: YAML, TOML, and JSON with per-value spans and serde support. |
| Part-of-speech tags | A Rust port of the `prose` v3.3.1 tagger that Vale uses (decision record 0001, decision 25). The binary embeds the model under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution and a notice that covers the model file only. |
| Spelling | `spellbook` with SCOWL and VarCon data |
| Code comments | `tree-sitter` with the language pack |
| HTML | `html5ever` |
| RST | A bundled docutils-to-HTML adapter in core |
| AsciiDoc | An experimental first-party extractor plugin that converts through asciidoctor to HTML |
| Discovery | `ignore` and `globset`. `.gitignore` support sits behind a setting. |
| Diff scope | `git` subprocess or `git2`, with `similar` |
| Config | A layer stack of our own: `toml_edit`, `saphyr`, serde, `schemars`. The `schematic` spike lost on provenance. |
| Errors | `thiserror` in libraries, `anyhow` in the binary, `annotate-snippets` for rendering |
| CLI | `clap`, `clap_complete`, `clap_mangen` |
| HTML report | `minijinja` |
| Paths, writes, locks | `etcetera`, `tempfile` persist, `fs4` |
| Downloads | `ureq`, `sha2`, `flate2`, `tar`, `zip`, with safe extraction |
| Updates | `update-informer`, plus `axoupdater` for installs made by our own installer |
| Signatures | `minisign-verify` for releases and plugins |
| LSP | `lsp-server` |
| Logging | `tracing`, enabled with `SLOPVAC_LOG` |

### Data and API schema

pydantic models defined the 2.x schema. In 3.0, Rust types generate the JSON Schema, which is published per API major version.

- **IDs:** namespaced as `<pack>:<id>`. Built-ins live in `core`. Short names still work where they are unambiguous.
- **Rules:**
  - A typed `match:` block (`tokens`, `pattern`, `substitution`, `metric`, `structure`, `capitalization`, `vocabulary`, `judgement`).
  - Fields for `exclude_blocks`, `contexts`, `applies_to`, and named exception detectors.
  - Test cases in the `vale test` style: `input`, `want`, `contains`, `absent`.
  - `tiers` is removed.
- **Profiles:** set gate thresholds and a severity shift only.
- **Styles:** ordered presets with `extends` and declared `conflicts`. The last listed style wins.
- **Genres:** data files with detection signals. A content type such as `how-to` is a genre that extends a genre. Diátaxis types are consumer content types.
- **Context tags:** `{kind, span, confidence, evidence}` from registered taggers. Taggers are declarative in data packs and code in plugins.
- **Terms:** `.slopvac/terms.toml`. Each term needs only `term`. `variants` and `kind` are optional.
- **Config:**
  - `slopvac.toml` with `schema_version = 3`, `extends`, `styles`, `packs`, `plugins`, `[[genres]]`, `[frontmatter]` policy, `[vale]` removed, `[guidance] level`, `[thresholds]`, and `[[overrides]]`.
  - The nearest config to each file applies.
  - Front matter is an allowed-fields layer under a `slopvac:` key.
- **Lint JSON v3:** `schema_version`, `notices`, per-document `genre` and config sources, and per-finding `pack`, `contexts`, and `end_line`.
- **Output formats:** `text`, `json`, `sarif`, `rdjsonl`, `codeclimate`, `junit`, `checkstyle`, `markdown`, `html`, and LSP diagnostics. Each rule has a stable documentation page that the formats link to.

### Layer order

From lowest priority to highest: core defaults, styles, the genre chain, `extends`, project config, matching `[[genres]]` and `[[overrides]]`, front matter, inline directives, CLI flags.
`--explain-config` prints the layer, the file, and the line for each value, and what the value overrode.

### Packs and plugins

- **Data packs** hold rules, styles, genres, terms, declarative taggers, and prime snippets. They contain no code. A `slopvac-pack.toml` manifest declares `slopvac_api`.
- **Code plugins** speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. Framing follows LSP. The `initialize` handshake exchanges capabilities. A Python SDK ships with them, and a conformance suite tests them.
  - Hook points: taggers, extractors, reporters, harness recipes, fixers, scorers, and model providers.
  - Python plugins run in their own environment.
- **Distribution:** OCI artifacts on GHCR or any registry is the primary channel. Release archives, local folders, and git pinned to a commit also work.
- **Lockfile:** `.slopvac/packs.lock` records the version, source, and digest.
- **Signatures:** minisign signatures ship as manifest layers. Publisher keys are listed in the index.
- **Trust:**
  - The plugin host refuses to load an untrusted code plugin. slopvac lists each one with the command that trusts it.
  - `slopvac plugins trust` records trust per content hash. Trust is an explicit command, not a prompt.
  - Agents and CI never trust on the user's behalf.
- **Commands:** `plugins sync`, `outdated`, `update`, `status`, `trust`, and `search`, which reads an index that a job rebuilds automatically. `pack new`, `validate`, `test`, and `publish` complete the set.

### Agents

- **prime:**
  - The base topic is about 250 words. It has one line per command and an index of topics.
  - Each topic is a terse checklist with its own index.
  - slopvac renders each topic from a Markdown file, against the config, at the detail that `[guidance] level` selects.
  - `.slopvac/PRIME.md` overrides a topic.
- **Setup:** `setup <harness>` supports `opencode`. The flags select the block, the skill, and the reviewer agent, and set the reviewer model. Skills follow the Agent Skills specification.
- **Review:**
  - Types are `mechanical`, `update`, and `rewrite`.
  - Fact checking covers changed claims only, with a scope that scales with the change. slopvac asks the user to confirm the scope when it would be exceeded.
  - Fact preservation uses lexical alignment and a literal diff.
  - The reviewer must use a different model from the author.
- **Model guidance:** prime and the docs list model recommendations per review type. The eval results generate the list.

### Distribution and release

- cargo-dist builds release archives, installers, and a Homebrew tap (`srobroek/homebrew-tap`).
- maturin wheels keep `uvx slopvac` as the documented default.
- Release candidates are `rc/vX.Y.Z-rc.N` tags cut on demand, with a provenance gate before stable. In 2.x, candidates build from each update to the release PR branch, wait for approval in the `pypi` environment, and get no tag or changelog entry.
- Releases carry minisign signatures. GitHub attestations, an SBOM, and an auditable binary come with each release.
- `slopvac self update` runs for installs made by our installer. Other installs print the matching upgrade command.
- The GitHub Action uses reviewdog with `reporter: auto`, or uploads SARIF. Its own annotation code is removed.
- MegaLinter and Trunk descriptors follow the release.

### Quality

- Tests: nextest, `cargo test --doc`, insta, and snapbox or trycmd.
- Lints: clippy with workspace lints, and rustfmt.
- Hygiene: cargo-deny, cargo-shear, typos, cargo-sort, Swatinem/rust-cache, and Dependabot for cargo.
- Hooks: prek.
- Added later: cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-mutants on the diff, fuzzing of parsers, CodeQL, gungraun benchmarks, and an MSRV check.

### Generated documentation

slopvac generates every reference document from code and data, and CI fails when a generated file is stale:

- API schemas from the Rust types: lint JSON, config, front matter, pack manifest, rules, styles, genres, terms, lockfile, and plugin protocol messages. Each schema is versioned per API major and published at a stable URL.
- One page per rule, with examples, exceptions, contexts, severity per profile and style, and provenance. Output formats link to these pages.
- One page per style preset and per genre or content type.
- The plugin protocol reference, the hook points, the pack manifest reference, and a page per pack.
- Rust API docs: crate docs in every `lib.rs`, `missing_docs` on library crates, rustdoc with warnings denied, and docs.rs for published crates.

### Evals

- An eval corpus lives in the repository as a manifest and a fetch script. It contains:
  - human text written before 2022;
  - LLM text that its publisher labels as model output;
  - human twins, where models write from human outlines;
  - seeded defects with clean controls;
  - rewrite pairs.
- Labels come from judges of two model families plus a human spot check.
- A paired bootstrap over documents measures each change.
- `just eval` runs an offline tier in CI, A/B comparisons between refs, and model comparisons.
- A precision ratchet blocks rule changes that lower precision beyond the noise.

### Migration from 2.x

- `uvx slopvac@latest prime migrate` runs the chain of migrations from the detected version.
- `docs/migrate-2-to-3.md` and `prime migrate` render from one source.
- `slopvac migrate` previews the changes, then rewrites the config with comments kept. It updates directive IDs and steering blocks. It compares findings before and after migration.
- 3.0 has no 2.x compatibility mode. It rejects a 2.x config with exit 2 and points to `slopvac migrate`. Removed flags, options, and hooks fail with an error, with no warning period.

## Release gate and risks

An adversarial review of this plan and its beads found these gaps. Each one now has a bead:

- **Compatibility:** a generated matrix of every 2.x command, flag, and behavior, with a disposition (preserve, migrate, or remove) and an owning bead. Installed-binary tests cover the preserved rows. stdin, `--diff-working-tree`, `--fix`, `reference`, `onboard`, `init`, `setup --remove`, and the published pre-commit hook IDs each have their own bead.
- **Golden suite modes:** reference parity pinned to a Python commit, Vale 3.24, and corpus hashes; 3.0 default-policy tests with reviewed deltas; and migration-preservation tests. The 2.x profiles have per-rule dispositions, so a separate bead maps them onto the 3.0 model.
- **Plugin security:** a threat model and an independent review before the plugin host and OCI client close. The review covers what the signature covers, publisher-key authority, key rotation, extraction limits, subprocess containment, and regex resource limits.
- **PCRE2 build policy:** pin version 10.43 or later, test JIT and non-JIT across Windows, macOS, glibc, and musl, and prove a match-limit mechanism.
- **POS tagger:** `harper-brill` failed its spike (`slopvac-8l4.3.10`): noun agreement 3.8% and 10.9% of words untagged. A Rust port of the `prose` tagger passed, with 99.1% exact tag match. Only the opt-in vocabulary blocklist check depends on POS. The binary embeds the model under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution and a share-alike notice for the model file only; the code keeps the project licence (`slopvac-8l4.3.23`).
- **Accuracy gate:** recall on seeded and adjudicated positives, false-positive rates on clean controls, and a held-out set, as well as precision.
- **Position contract:** byte spans, line and column bases, and per-format conversions, including LSP UTF-16. Agree these before fixes and suggestions ship.
- **RST:** stays in core through a bundled docutils adapter. AsciiDoc is new and experimental.
- **Performance:** budgets for the installed binary, measured before they gate releases.
- **Policies:** network and privacy, accessibility, and API lifecycle. Breaking changes happen at major versions, with no deprecation windows.
- **Release readiness:** one gate bead that the stable release depends on, separate from building candidates.
- **Interim status:** no 2.x release ships, so the issues get status and workarounds now.

The review also proposed a smaller 3.0.0 that moves the new platforms to 3.1. The decision, made 2026-11-14, is to keep the full scope in 3.0.0. Every programme bead outside the backlog carries the `release:3.0.0` label. The release-readiness gate still applies to the whole scope.

## Order of work

1. Rule-data fixes in the Python reference, and repository hygiene.
2. 3.0 contract: schemas, plugin protocol, golden suite, fixtures.
3. Rust engine crates, behind the golden suite.
4. Config, front matter, terms, genres, styles, and context tagger.
5. CLI, output formats, LSP, prime, and setup.
6. Packs and plugins: protocol, OCI, trust, signatures, and first-party packs.
7. Diagrams, experimental.
8. Distribution, release candidates, and migration.
9. Evals and the precision ratchet. These start in step 2 and continue in parallel.

## Backlog

- A WASM build.
- Languages other than English.
- D2 and Structurizr extractors.
- An optional MCP wrapper.
- Sigstore and attestation verification in Rust.
- A model2vec plugin.

# Lint report schema

`slopvac lint --format json` writes one report that validates against
[`schemas/v3/lint-report.schema.json`](../../schemas/v3/lint-report.schema.json). The
bead is slopvac-8l4.2.2. This page states what the schema cannot: where each 2.x key
went, and the rules a consumer relies on. Field descriptions live in the schema.

## Read a report

- `schema_version` is 3. Lint JSON jumps from 1 to 3, so no report carries 2.
- Consumers must branch on `notices[].code` and `unchecked[].code`, never on the message
  text. A code keeps its meaning for the whole 3.x line. Codes are kebab-case.
- `slopvac_version` names the tool build. It does not signal a schema change.
- The schema is strict, because it is the producer contract. Slopvac writes only reports
  that validate, and its own tests check that. A consumer must ignore unknown fields, as
  [the field policy](policies.md) requires, so a later 3.x release can add keys. Keys that
  start with `x-` are reserved for extensions and have no meaning.
- Minor releases add keys and codes only. A removal or a type change waits for 4.0.
- `line`, `column`, `end_line` and `end_column` are the display position. `span` is the
  byte range, from [`Span`](../../schemas/v3/common.schema.json#/$defs/Span). A finding
  with no source range, such as a document-wide metric, omits `span`, `end_line` and
  `end_column` together.
- `fix.edits` hold [`Edit`](../../schemas/v3/common.schema.json#/$defs/Edit) values.
  Their byte ranges address the original text and never overlap.
- `gate` is the verdict for one document under its profile. Exit codes still come from
  the run: 0 passes, 1 means that a gate failed, 2 means that the run was incomplete.

## New in v3

These keys have no 2.x counterpart.

- Root: `notices`, replacing `notes`.
- Document: `genre` with its `reasons`, `contexts_seen`, `config_sources`
  ([`ConfigSource`](../../schemas/v3/common.schema.json#/$defs/ConfigSource)) and `gate`.
- Finding: `pack`, `span`, `end_line`, `contexts`, `fix` and `provenance`
  ([`RuleProvenance`](../../schemas/v3/common.schema.json#/$defs/RuleProvenance)).

## 2.x key dispositions

A 2.x key is `preserve`d, `rename`d or `remove`d. 3.0 has no deprecation window and no
compatibility mode, so a renamed or removed key is gone at release. Run
`tests/contract/test_lint_report_2x_keys.py` to check that this table matches the 2.x
models in `slopvac.report` and `slopvac.model`.

| 2.x key | Fate | v3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LintReport.schema_version` | preserve | The value moves from 1 to 3. A reader that pins 1 rejects a v3 report, which is intended. |
| `LintReport.version` | rename | Becomes `slopvac_version`, so no one reads it as a schema version. |
| `LintReport.summary` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `LintReport.documents` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `LintReport.notes` | rename | Becomes `notices`. Each entry changes from a string to a Notice with a stable `code`. The key is always present, where 2.x omitted `notes` when empty. |
| `RunSummary.documents` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.words` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.findings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.errors` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.warnings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.suggestions` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.score` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.passed` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.categories` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.ai_register` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `RunSummary.prose` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.category` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.findings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.errors` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.warnings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.suggestions` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `CategorySummary.score` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.path` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.profile` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.words` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.sentences` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.paragraphs` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.findings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.categories` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.total_findings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.errors` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.warnings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.suggestions` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.score` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.ai_register` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.prose` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `DocumentScore.passed` | rename | Becomes `gate.passed`. |
| `DocumentScore.failure_reasons` | rename | Becomes `gate.reasons`. A failed gate lists at least one reason. A passed gate lists none. |
| `DocumentScore.unchecked` | preserve | Same key. Entries change from strings to Notices with a stable `code`. |
| `CategoryScore.category` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.findings` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.errors` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.warnings` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.suggestions` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.gating_per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.budget` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.score` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `CategoryScore.over_budget` | preserve | Unchanged. `budget` stays nullable. |
| `Finding.path` | remove | Redundant with the owning document's `path`. A consumer that needs it reads the parent document. |
| `Finding.line` | preserve | Same keys. `column` and `end_column` now follow the position rules of slopvac-8l4.2.11. `end_column` is present only with `span`. |
| `Finding.column` | preserve | Same keys. `column` and `end_column` now follow the position rules of slopvac-8l4.2.11. `end_column` is present only with `span`. |
| `Finding.end_column` | preserve | Same keys. `column` and `end_column` now follow the position rules of slopvac-8l4.2.11. `end_column` is present only with `span`. |
| `Finding.rule_id` | preserve | Same key. The value uses the form `<pack>:<id>`, such as `core:orwell.not-un`. 2.x emitted `<category>.<id>`. |
| `Finding.category` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `Finding.severity` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `Finding.message` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `Finding.ai_signal` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `Finding.matched_text` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `Finding.replacement` | rename | Becomes `fix.edits`, a list of byte-range edits instead of one replacement string. |
| `Finding.ste_ref` | remove | Rule metadata, not finding data. `slopvac explain` prints it, and `provenance` names the pack and source. |
| `Finding.orwell_ref` | remove | Rule metadata, not finding data. `slopvac explain` prints it, and `provenance` names the pack and source. |
| `AiRegisterSummary.findings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `AiRegisterSummary.errors` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `AiRegisterSummary.warnings` | preserve | Unchanged. |
| `AiRegisterSummary.per_100_words` | preserve | Unchanged. |

## Consumers to migrate

These 2.x readers and writers use the old keys. The 3.0 output beads own the move:
slopvac-8l4.12.2 for the formats and slopvac-8l4.13.6 for the action.

- `action_entry.py` reads the JSON report. Owner: slopvac-8l4.13.6.
- The SARIF builder in `report.py`. Owner: slopvac-8l4.12.2.
- `html.py`. Owner: slopvac-8l4.12.2.
- The annotation output in `pipeline.py`. Owner: slopvac-8l4.12.2.

## Conformance

`schemas/v3/conformance/lint-report/` holds the corpus. `valid/multi-document.json` is a
realistic three-document report. Each file under `invalid/` fails at the pointer named in
`cases.toml`. The corpus is the snapshot: schemas generated from the Rust types must
accept and reject the same files.

# Slopvac 3.0 config and front matter

Status: contract for 3.0. Bead `slopvac-8l4.2.5`. Plan: [slopvac-3.md](../design/slopvac-3.md). Decision: [architecture record 0001](../design/0001-slopvac-3-architecture.md), section 20.

The schemas are [`config.schema.json`](../../schemas/v3/config.schema.json) for `slopvac.toml` and [`frontmatter.schema.json`](../../schemas/v3/frontmatter.schema.json) for the `slopvac:` block. Field meanings live in the schema `description` fields. This document states what the schemas cannot: layer order, merge rules, discovery, and the move from 2.x.

Each statement is a **2.x behavior** with its source in `packages/slopvac-lint/src/slopvac/config.py`, or a **3.0 requirement** with an owning bead.

## 1. Layers

### 1.1 Order

Lowest priority first. A higher layer wins.

| # | Layer | `ConfigSource.layer` | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Core defaults | `core` | Rule definitions, built-in profiles, default `exclude` |
| 2 | Styles | `style` | The `styles` list, in order. The last listed wins. |
| 3 | Genre chain | `genre` | The settings of the document's genre and the genres it extends |
| 4 | `extends` | `extends` | Extended configs, in list order. A later entry wins. |
| 5 | Project config | `project` | The nearest `slopvac.toml` |
| 6 | Matching `[[genres]]` and `[[overrides]]` | `override` | Blocks in file order. The last writer of a field wins. |
| 7 | Front matter | `front-matter` | The `slopvac:` block, limited by `[frontmatter] allow` |
| 8 | Inline directives | `directive` | Directives in the document |
| 9 | CLI flags | `cli` | Flags such as `--profile` |

The order comes from the plan, section "Layer order". Environment switches (`SLOPVAC_OFFLINE`) are source `env`. They only set sticky values, so they sit outside the order (section 1.3).

**2.x behavior.** The chain had three layers: the profile, the top-level tables, and each matching `[[overrides]]` block in file order (`config.py`, module docstring and `resolve_for`). Front matter, genres, styles and `extends` did not exist.

### 1.2 Merge rules

**3.0 requirement.** A higher layer patches a lower one field by field.

- A scalar replaces the lower value. This covers `profile` fields and `locale`.
- A map merges by key. This covers `rules`, `categories`, `thresholds` and `terms`. A higher layer that names one key leaves the others alone.
- A list replaces the lower list. This covers `exclude`, `styles`, `terms.allow`, `terms.files`, `terms.blocklists` and `files`. A project that wants the default `exclude` plus one pattern restates the defaults. This matches 2.x, where a user `exclude` replaced the default list (`Config.exclude`) and an override `locale.allow` replaced the project's.
- An explicit threshold survives a profile change. The resolver picks the final profile across all layers. Then it applies each `thresholds` entry on top, layer by layer (`resolve_for`, which also does this in 2.x).
- `severity_shift` moves the levels that come from rule definitions, styles and the genre chain. A level that a `rules` or `categories` entry sets is final, and the shift leaves it alone. `off` stays `off`, and the result clamps at `suggestion` and `error`. The numbers for each built-in profile are in the profile mapping (`slopvac-8l4.2.10`).
- A higher layer cannot reset a field to unset. It sets a value.

Sticky settings break the rule. `network.offline = true` in any layer, from any file in an `extends` chain, from the `SLOPVAC_OFFLINE` variable or from `--offline`, makes the run offline. No layer can set it back. See [policies.md](policies.md), section 1.3.

Scopes that apply to one file combine in file order, not by specificity. A glob that is more general and later in the file wins over a narrower one earlier. 2.x works this way (`resolve_for`), and 3.0 keeps it because file order needs no ranking of globs.

### 1.3 Project-wide tables

`guidance`, `network`, `review`, `packs`, `plugins`, `styles`, `extends`, `frontmatter`, `mode` and `exclude` apply to the whole run or to file selection. They are not part of the `Settings` patch. An `[[overrides]]` or `[[genres]]` block that names one is an error, and so is a front matter field of that name. 2.x already rejected `guidance` in an override (`Override._reject_guidance`). 3.0 extends the rule to the other tables.

### 1.4 Provenance

Every resolved value carries a `ConfigSource` (`common.schema.json#/$defs/ConfigSource`):

- `layer` is one of the names in section 1.1, or `env`.
- `file` is the path relative to the project root. A value from a pack uses `pack:<id>/<path>`. A `core`, `cli` or `env` value has no file.
- `line` and `column` are one-based and point at the key that set the value. For front matter, they count from the start of the document file, not from the start of the block.
- A `[[genres]]` or `[[overrides]]` value uses layer `override`. The report names the block by its index.

`slopvac lint --explain-config` prints the layer, file, line and column of each value and the value it overrode. 2.x printed only a label such as `overrides[0] (docs/**)` (`provenance` in `resolve_for`). Owners: `slopvac-8l4.4.2` for the stack, `slopvac-8l4.4.7` for diagnostics.

## 2. Nearest config

**2.x behavior.** `find_config` runs once from the working directory (`cli.py`, `config_path or find_config(Path.cwd())`). It checks `slopvac.toml`, then `.slopvac.toml`, then a `[tool.slopvac]` table in `pyproject.toml`, in each directory from the start upward. It stops after the first directory that contains `.git`. The docstring of `config.py` says discovery walks up from each target file. The code does not: one config applies to every file in the run.

**3.0 requirement.**

1. For each file, start in the file's directory. Walk up, one directory at a time.
2. The first directory that holds `slopvac.toml` supplies the config. Call it the nearest config.
3. A directory that holds `.git`, as a directory or a file, ends the walk after its own `slopvac.toml` is checked. The walk never leaves the repository.
4. A file without a `slopvac.toml` on its path uses the core defaults.
5. Only the nearest config applies. A parent config does not merge in on its own. Use `extends` to inherit.
6. `--config <path>` skips discovery and applies that one file to every file in the run. Its directory is the root for globs.
7. Input from `--stdin` uses the nearest config of the working directory.
8. A config pattern in `exclude`, `files` or a negated form matches the path relative to the directory of the nearest config. A file outside that directory matches no override. The 2.x fallback to the bare file name is removed.
9. Path values for files (`terms.files`, `terms.blocklists`, a local `packs` source, `extends`) are relative to the file that holds the value.
10. The walk finds only `slopvac.toml`. A `.slopvac.toml` file or a `[tool.slopvac]` table that the walk meets is a 2.x config and is rejected (section 5).

Resolution is cached per directory, so a run over many files reads each config once.

### 2.1 `extends`

- Entries apply in list order, and a later entry wins. The extending file wins over all of them.
- An entry is a path relative to the extending file, or `<pack>:<name>` for a config that a pack ships.
- An extended file is a v3 config. It must carry `schema_version = 3`. It may extend others.
- A cycle is an error that names the chain: `config-extends-cycle`.
- The nearest config decides `exclude` globs and override globs, wherever the pattern was written.

## 3. Front matter

The block is the mapping under the `slopvac:` key of a document's front matter. Front matter in YAML (`---`), TOML (`+++`) or JSON is read, and the block has the same shape in each. The schema validates the parsed mapping. Conformance instances are YAML.

- `v` is required and equals 3, the same number as `schema_version`. A larger value is an error that names the versions supported and the upgrade command.
- The fields are `genre`, `profile`, `locale`, `thresholds`, `categories`, `rules` and `terms.allow`. No other key is allowed, and a misspelling is an error at its line and column.
- `[frontmatter] allow` in the project config sets which fields take effect. The default is `genre`, `locale` and `terms`, so a document can weaken its own gate only after the project opts in. A field outside the list is an error: `config-frontmatter-field-denied`. Slopvac reports it every time.
- `[frontmatter] enabled = false` makes `slopvac:` ordinary data. Slopvac neither reads nor validates it.
- Keys outside `slopvac:` are the document's own and are never checked.
- Keys that start with `x-` are ignored inside the block.

## 4. Other config rules

- Every `slopvac.toml` carries `schema_version = 3`. A file without it, or with 2, is a 2.x config.
- Unknown keys are errors with file, line and column, and the nearest valid key. Keys that start with `x-` are ignored. The exception is a map keyed by rule or category name (`rules`, `categories`). Its keys are data, so `x-` has no special meaning there ([policies.md](policies.md), section 3.3).
- A rule or category key is qualified (`<pack>:<id>`) or a bare name that is unambiguous across the active packs. An ambiguous or unknown name is an error from the resolver. The schema checks only the form.
- `rules` takes a bare level. The 2.x table form `[rules."x"] severity = "off"` is not valid, because a level is the only field.
- Two blocks in `[[overrides]]` or `[[genres]]` with the same `files` set are an error: `config-duplicate-scope`. This keeps `Config._reject_duplicate_scopes` from 2.x. The patterns compare as a set after whitespace is trimmed.
- A `[[genres]]` block assigns a genre to the files it matches and patches their settings. The genre itself is defined in a genre file (`genre.schema.json`, owned by another bead).
- `exclude` and `files` patterns use gitignore semantics through the same engine as 2.x. A leading `!` negates, and the last matching pattern wins.
- A threshold absent from a profile and from every layer is unset, and its gate does not run.

## 5. Moving from 2.x

3.0 invalidates 2.x configs. No compatibility mode exists, and there is no warning period. Section 3.7 of [policies.md](policies.md) states the policy.

- A config with no `schema_version`, or with 2, makes every command that reads config exit 2 with `config-legacy-version`. The error names the file and points to `slopvac migrate`. Nothing is linted.
- Discovery treats a `.slopvac.toml` file and a `[tool.slopvac]` table as 2.x configs and fails the same way.
- `slopvac migrate` is the only path. It previews every change and then rewrites the file with comments kept. It compares findings before and after.
- A setting with no 3.0 equivalent stops the migration with `config-legacy-dropped`. The error names the key, the file, the line and the reason. `migrate` writes nothing until the user removes or rewrites that setting. It reports every such setting in one run.

Owners for the behavior: `slopvac-8l4.16.1` for `migrate`, `slopvac-8l4.4.5` for the version check.

### 5.1 Dispositions

- **preserve**: the key and its meaning carry over. `migrate` copies the value.
- **migrate**: 3.0 has the setting under a new key or form. `migrate` rewrites it.
- **remove**: 3.0 has no equivalent. `migrate` fails with `config-legacy-dropped`, except where the table says the removal is lossless.

### 5.2 Mapping table

Rule and category names change with the pack model. `migrate` maps a 2.x name such as `prose-format.no-unicode-dash` to its 3.0 qualified id through the rename table in the binary. A name with no entry stops the migration. The table is part of the profile and rule mapping (`slopvac-8l4.2.10`). The rows below call this "rename".

| 2.x setting | Disposition | 3.0 | `slopvac migrate` |
|---|---|---|---|
| File `slopvac.toml` | preserve | `slopvac.toml` | Adds `schema_version = 3`. |
| File `.slopvac.toml` | migrate | `slopvac.toml` in the same directory | Renames the file. Stops if a `slopvac.toml` exists there, because 2.x ignored the dotfile in that case. |
| Table `[tool.slopvac]` in `pyproject.toml` | migrate | `slopvac.toml` next to `pyproject.toml` | Writes the new file and deletes the table from `pyproject.toml`, keeping its comments. |
| No version field | migrate | `schema_version = 3` | Adds it. |
| `mode` | preserve | `mode` | Copies it. |
| `profile` | preserve | `profile`, as a name | Copies the name. What a tier does changes: it sets thresholds and a severity shift only. The rule defaults it carried move to styles and rule definitions (`slopvac-8l4.2.10`). |
| `exclude` | preserve | `exclude` | Copies the list. A list replaces the default, as in 2.x. |
| Negated globs in `exclude` | preserve | `!pattern` | Copies them. Order matters and is kept. |
| `categories.<name>` as a bare level | preserve | `categories.<name>` | Renames the category. |
| `categories.<name>.severity` | preserve | `categories.<name>.severity`, or a bare level when it is the only field | Renames the category. |
| `categories.<name>.minimum_severity` | preserve | same key, `off` included | Renames the category. In 2.x, `off` sets no floor (`engine.py`, the rank test skips it), and 3.0 gives it the same meaning. |
| `categories.<name>.max_per_100_words` | preserve | same key | Renames the category. |
| `categories.<name>.weight` | preserve | same key | Renames the category. |
| `rules.<id>` as a bare level | preserve | `rules.<qualified id>` | Renames the rule. |
| `rules.<id>.severity` as a table | migrate | `rules.<qualified id>` as a bare level | Renames the rule and writes the bare level. |
| `thresholds.max_total_per_100_words` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `thresholds.max_errors` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `thresholds.max_warnings` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `thresholds.min_score` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `thresholds.max_unicode_dashes` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `locale.default` | migrate | `locale` | Moves the value up one level. |
| `locale.allow` | migrate | `terms.allow` | Moves the list. The words still skip the spelling check. |
| `vocabulary.path` | migrate | `terms.blocklists = [<path>]` | Keeps the path and checks that the file still loads. The entries keep `word`, `pos` and `reason`. |
| `vale.enabled = false` | remove, lossless | none | Deletes the table and lists the deletion in the summary. Vale is gone in 3.0 (architecture record 0001, decision 2). |
| `vale.enabled = true` | remove | none | Fails with `config-legacy-dropped`. |
| `vale.binary` | remove | none | Fails, unless `vale.enabled = false` is set in the same table. |
| `vale.config` | remove | none | Fails, unless `vale.enabled = false` is set in the same table. |
| `vale.styles` | remove | none | Fails, unless `vale.enabled = false` is set in the same table. |
| `guidance.write` | preserve | `guidance.write` | Copies it. |
| `guidance.review` | preserve | `guidance.review` | Copies it. |
| `guidance.review_depth` | preserve | `guidance.review_depth` | Copies it. |
| `guidance.report` | preserve | `guidance.report` | Copies it. |
| None (new) | none | `guidance.level` | Not written. The default is `standard`. |
| `overrides[].files` | preserve | `overrides[].files` | Copies it, negated globs included. Patterns now match from the nearest config's directory. |
| `overrides[].profile` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `overrides[].categories` | preserve | same key | Renames the categories. |
| `overrides[].rules` | preserve | same key | Renames the rules and writes bare levels. |
| `overrides[].thresholds` | preserve | same key | Copies it. |
| `overrides[].locale.default` | migrate | `overrides[].locale` | Moves the value up one level. |
| `overrides[].locale.allow` | migrate | `overrides[].terms.allow` | Moves the list. |
| `overrides[].vocabulary.path` | migrate | `overrides[].terms.blocklists` | Same as the project-level row. |
| `overrides[].vale` | remove | none | Same rules as the project-level `vale` rows. |
| `overrides[].guidance` | preserve (rejected) | rejected | 2.x already refused it. The error carries over. |
| Unknown keys rejected (`extra="forbid"`) | preserve | unknown keys are errors | The error gains line and column. |
| Duplicate override scopes rejected | preserve | `config-duplicate-scope` | Fails on the same inputs. |
| Override cascade in file order, last writer wins | preserve | layer 6 | Order is kept. |
| One config chosen from the working directory | migrate | nearest config per file | No rewrite. The effect is described in section 2. |
| Override match on the bare file name outside the root | remove | none | No rewrite. The file matches no override. |
| Table `[tool.slopvac]` and `.slopvac.toml` discovery | remove | none | Section 2, rule 10. |

The `minimum_severity` row has one 2.x quirk. `CategorySettings` declares the field twice. The two declarations are identical, so the duplicate has no effect, and `migrate` ignores it.

## 6. Conformance

The conformance corpus is the lasting golden. Generated schemas must accept and reject the same files.

- `schemas/v3/conformance/config/valid/` holds TOML configs: a minimal one, one that uses every table, and one in the shape `migrate` writes.
- `schemas/v3/conformance/config/invalid/` holds one defect per file. Each is mapped to a JSON pointer in `cases.toml`. The cases cover a missing or old `schema_version`, a 2.x `[vale]` table, unknown keys, bad levels, the 2.x table form of a rule, a `guidance` table inside an override, and an unqualified pack id.
- `schemas/v3/conformance/frontmatter/` holds YAML front matter, including a document with other keys, a document with no `slopvac:` key, and an `x-` key inside the block.
- `schemas/v3/conformance/common/` holds `ConfigSource` instances for each layer shape.

A schema checks form only. These behaviors need the resolver and have their own tests there: ambiguous rule names, duplicate scopes, `extends` cycles, denied front matter fields, and sticky offline mode.

# Migrate from 2.x to 3.0

Slopvac 3.0 has no 2.x compatibility mode. A 2.x config makes every command that reads config exit 2 with `config-legacy-version`. Nothing is linted until you migrate. `slopvac migrate` is the only path.

Migrations chain from the version it detects. One step exists: 2.x to 3.0. A config with no `schema_version`, or with `schema_version = 2`, starts at that step. A config with `schema_version = 3` needs no migration, and `slopvac migrate` reports it as already migrated.

## 1. Find the 2.x surfaces

Look for these in the project:

- `.slopvac.toml`, or a `slopvac.toml` with no `schema_version = 3`.
- A `[tool.slopvac]` table in `pyproject.toml`.
- `slopvac-allow` comments whose `rule=` value has no pack prefix, such as `rule=prose-format.no-unicode-dash`.
- Steering blocks between `<!-- slopvac:begin -->` and `<!-- slopvac:end -->` in agent instruction files.
- Scripts, CI jobs and hooks that use a removed flag, command, action input or hook id (section 6).

## 2. Preview

```sh
slopvac migrate
```

The command prints a diff of every file it would change and exits 0. It writes nothing. It lints the project before and after, and lists the rules whose finding counts change.

## 3. Resolve blockers

Some 2.x settings have no 3.0 equivalent. The command stops with exit 2 and prints one `config-legacy-dropped` line for each, with the file, line, key and reason. It lists all of them in one run and writes nothing.

Common causes:

- `[vale]` with `enabled = true`, or with `binary`, `config` or `styles` and no `enabled = false`. Vale is removed in 3.0. Delete the table or set `enabled = false`.
- A rule or category name that is not in the rename table.
- A key 3.0 does not know, or a `guidance` table inside an override.

Edit the file, then run the preview again.

## 4. Apply

```sh
slopvac migrate --write
```

The command copies each file it replaces to `.slopvac-migrate-backup` and then rewrites it. Config comments and key order stay. It does the following:

- Moves `.slopvac.toml` and `[tool.slopvac]` into `slopvac.toml`, and adds `schema_version = 3`. Other content in `pyproject.toml` stays.
- Renames categories and rules to their 3.0 names, and writes a rule that had only a `severity` as a bare level.
- Moves `locale.default` to `locale`, `locale.allow` to `terms.allow`, and `vocabulary.path` to `terms.blocklists`.
- Deletes a `[vale]` table that has `enabled = false`.
- Qualifies the rule id in each `slopvac-allow` comment. Comments inside code fences and code spans are examples and stay.
- Replaces each steering block with the 3.0 text.

The command stops if one directory holds more than one of `slopvac.toml`, `.slopvac.toml` and `[tool.slopvac]`. 2.x read only one of them. Remove the ones you do not use and run again.

To keep the 2.x vocabulary behavior, add `--preserve-behavior`. It adds the STE style to `styles`.

## 5. Verify and undo

Run `slopvac lint` on the project. Compare the result with the per-rule report from the preview.

To undo a write, run `slopvac migrate --restore`. It puts the backed-up files back, removes the files the write created, and deletes the backup directory. If you keep the migration, delete `.slopvac-migrate-backup`.

A second `slopvac migrate` finds nothing to change.

## 6. Removed in 3.0

These 2.x surfaces fail with exit 2. Update scripts, CI and hooks by hand. `slopvac migrate` does not edit them.

| Surface | What to do |
|---|---|
| `--profile` on `lint`, `rules`, `explain` and `init` | Set the style preset in `slopvac.toml`. |
| `--rules-dir` on `lint`, `rules`, `explain`, `prime` and `reference` | Declare a local pack in `slopvac.toml`. |
| `--no-vale`, `doctor --binary` | Delete the flag. Vale is removed. |
| `--comments` | Use `--mode code-comments`. |
| `compile` and its options (`--outdir`, `--profile`, `--config`, `--rules-dir`, `--no-validate`, `--format`) | Delete the call. Compiled Vale styles are removed. |
| `cache` and its options (`--prune`, `--all`) | Delete the call. The Vale cache is removed. |
| Action inputs `profile`, `vale`, `vale-version` and `rules-dir` | Delete the input. Set the style preset and packs in `slopvac.toml`. |
| Hook id `slopvac-no-vale` | Delete the hook. |
